paragraphs.title: God’s Salvation Revealed to Israel and the Nations

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “O sing unto the LORD a new song.”
easy.q: What is the psalmist told to sing unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “for he hath done marvellous things.”

answers: Only the people of the sea
easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “He hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel.”
easy.q: Toward whom did the LORD remember His mercy and truth?

answers: All the ends of the earth
medium.explanation: The verse says, “all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.”
medium.q: Who has seen the salvation of our God?

answers: The LORD has done marvellous things and brought salvation
The sound of the harp alone
The roaring of the sea and rivers
medium.explanation: The new song responds to the LORD’s marvellous works and salvation.
medium.q: What is the reason given for singing a new song?

answers: Far away from the house of Israel
medium.explanation: The LORD’s righteousness was openly shown before the nations.
medium.q: What does “in the sight of the heathen” mean?

answers: The ends of the earth judge Israel
God’s salvation for Israel is seen throughout the world
challenge.explanation: God’s mercy toward Israel is revealed so that all the ends of the earth see His salvation.
challenge.q: What relationship is described between Israel and the ends of the earth?

answers: The musical instruments of the people
challenge.explanation: The right hand and holy arm represent the LORD’s power in gaining the victory.
challenge.q: What does the mention of the LORD’s “right hand” and “holy arm” emphasize?

answers: Because the sea began to roar
Because He has done marvellous things and made His salvation known
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s wonderful works and revealed salvation call for renewed praise.
challenge.q: Why is a new song appropriate after the LORD’s work?

paragraphs.title: A Universal Call to Song and Music

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all the earth.”
easy.q: Who is called to make a joyful noise unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “Sing unto the LORD with the harp.”
Verse 6 mentions “trumpets and sound of cornet.”
easy.q: Which instruments of the wind are mentioned?

answers: From voices and the harp to trumpets and the cornet
From the cornet to the harp and then to silence
From the sea to the rivers and mountains
medium.explanation: The passage moves from singing and the harp to trumpets and the cornet.
medium.q: How does the musical celebration build through these verses?

answers: Before the inhabitants of the earth
medium.explanation: Verse 6 says, “make a joyful noise before the LORD, the King.”
medium.q: Before whom are the people to make a joyful noise?

medium.explanation: The command to rejoice means to express gladness in praise.

answers: The invitation to praise is universal, not limited to one group
Only the earth itself can play music
The song is intended only for distant nations
challenge.explanation: The whole earth is invited to make a joyful noise, rejoice, and sing praise.
challenge.q: What does the call to “all the earth” show?

answers: The expansion and strengthening of praise
A separation between people and the LORD
challenge.explanation: Singing and instruments join together to create an enlarged celebration of praise.
challenge.q: What is suggested by combining voices with musical instruments?

challenge.explanation: Verse 6 calls Him “the LORD, the King.”
challenge.q: How is the LORD described in connection with the music?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof.”
easy.q: What does the sea and its fulness do?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “Let the floods clap their hands.”
The verse says, “let the hills be joyful together.”

answers: The sea, the world, the floods, and the hills
Only the inhabitants of the earth
medium.explanation: The passage personifies the sea, the world, the floods, and the hills as joining the celebration.
medium.q: What joins in the song besides human beings?

medium.explanation: The floods clap their hands, while the hills are joyful together.
medium.q: What relationship is shown between the floods and the hills?

answers: The people who live in the world
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the inhabitants of the world.
medium.q: What does “they that dwell therein” refer to?

challenge.explanation: The sea roars, the floods clap, and the hills rejoice, portraying creation as joining praise.
challenge.q: What central idea comes from the description of the sea, floods, and hills?

answers: It limits praise to musical instruments
It transfers praise only to Israel
It includes the whole created world
challenge.explanation: The call to praise extends beyond people to the natural world.
challenge.q: How does the description of nature expand the earlier call to sing?

challenge.explanation: The verse pictures the floods clapping their hands.
challenge.q: Which human action is attributed to the floods?

paragraphs.title: God Judges the World with Justice

easy.q: Before whom are all the sounds directed?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “for he cometh to judge the earth.”

answers: With the power of the sea
With the sound of the cornet
easy.explanation: The verse says, “with righteousness shall he judge the world.”
easy.q: With what shall the LORD judge the world?

medium.explanation: The verse says He will judge “the world, and the people.”
The verse emphasizes righteousness and equity in His judgment.
medium.q: What qualities describe the LORD’s judgment?

medium.explanation: Equity means fairness and upright judgment.
medium.q: What does “equity” mean in this context?

answers: The praise takes place before the LORD who judges
challenge.explanation: The voices of praise are heard before the LORD, who comes to judge the earth.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the singing and the judgment in the final verse?

answers: That joy is unrelated to God’s actions
That praise stands before righteous judgment
challenge.explanation: The celebration leads to the LORD’s presence and His righteous judgment.
challenge.q: What does the movement from rejoicing creation to divine judgment emphasize?

answers: The world is judged with righteousness and the people with equity
The world is judged with roaring and the people with a harp
challenge.explanation: The verse says the LORD judges the world with righteousness and the people with equity.
challenge.q: How are the judgment of the world and the judgment of the people described?
